topicName: Continuous Integration Setup (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Parallelization)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Continuous Integration Setup for Cypress with GitHub Actions and GitLab CI"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Setting up Continuous Integration (CI) for Cypress ensures your end-to-end tests run reliably on every commit and pull request. This tutorial covers setting up CI pipelines in both GitHub Actions and GitLab CI, complete with test parallelization to drastically reduce execution time."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A project configured with Cypress."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Cypress Cloud account (required for parallelization)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of YAML syntax."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"GitHub Actions: Basic Configuration"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To run Cypress tests in GitHub Actions, create a workflow file at .github/workflows/ci.yml in your repository."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"name: Cypress CI

on: [push]

jobs:
  cypress-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Cypress run
        uses: cypress-io/github-action@v6
        with:
          build: npm run build
          start: npm start"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"GitHub Actions: Parallelization"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To split your test suite across multiple machine instances, use the strategy.matrix feature along with your CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"name: Cypress Parallel CI

on: [push]

jobs:
  cypress-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        containers: [1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Cypress tests
        uses: cypress-io/github-action@v6
        with:
          parallel: true
          group: UI Tests
          record: true
        env:
          CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY: ${{ secrets.CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"GitLab CI: Basic Configuration"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"For GitLab CI, create a .gitlab-ci.yml file in the root of your repository using the official Cypress base images."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"stages:
  - test

cypress-test:
  stage: test
  image: cypress/included:13.6.0
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npx cypress run"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"GitLab CI: Parallelization"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitLab CI makes parallelization straightforward via the parallel keyword. Pass the record and parallel flags to the Cypress command."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"stages:
  - test

cypress-parallel:
  stage: test
  image: cypress/included:13.6.0
  parallel: 3
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npx cypress run --record --parallel --group "GitLab Parallel Group"
  variables:
    CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY: $CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for CI"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always cache your npm dependencies and the Cypress binary to speed up pipeline initialization."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Store sensitive keys like CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY securely in repository secrets or CI environment variables."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use fail-fast: false in matrix configurations so that a failure in one machine does not immediately cancel running jobs on other machines."}]
